; A first program for TEC-OS. Build it
; with TAS SAMPLE. Run it with SAMPLE.
;
; Say hello through CP/M BDOS, then
; check for the TEC-OS ABI 5 table.
; Print the screen size, write to LCD
; row 2, show 123456 and beep.

; TEC-OS's table and service numbers, by
; the names abi.inc gives them. "TNA",
; then the major version

ABITAB EQU $C003

; the major version this speaks: 5

ABIMAJ EQU $C006

; CALL here with the service in C

ABICALL EQU $C008
TNINFO EQU 0     ; -> L = columns, H =
                 ; rows
[more]

; AREA: print the size of the program area in bytes, in decimal.
BDOS	EQU	$0005

	ORG	$0100
	LD	HL,($0006)	; the first byte above the area
	LD	DE,$0100	; the area's first byte
	OR	A		; clear carry for the subtraction
	SBC	HL,DE		; HL = the size in bytes
	CALL	PUTDEC
	LD	DE,BYTES	; the text after the number
	LD	C,9		; BDOS function 9: print a string
	JP	BDOS		; print, and return from there

; PUTDEC: print HL in decimal, always as five digits. Takes HL.
; Returns nothing. Changes AF, BC, DE and HL.
PUTDEC:	LD	BC,-10000	; the ten-thousands digit
	CALL	DIGIT
	LD	BC,-1000	; the thousands, from what is left
	CALL	DIGIT
	LD	BC,-100		; the hundreds
	CALL	DIGIT
	LD	BC,-10		; the tens
	CALL	DIGIT
	LD	BC,-1		; the units: fall into DIGIT

; DIGIT: print how many times a power of ten goes into HL. Takes the
; negative of the power in BC and the number in HL. Returns the
; remainder in HL. Changes AF, BC and DE.
DIGIT:	LD	A,'0'-1		; one below the character for 0
DLOOP:	INC	A		; the next digit
	ADD	HL,BC		; take off one power of ten
	JR	C,DLOOP		; carry: HL is still 0 or more
	SBC	HL,BC		; one too many: add the power back
	PUSH	HL		; function 2 changes the registers
	LD	E,A
	LD	C,2		; BDOS function 2: print E
	CALL	BDOS
	POP	HL
	RET

BYTES:	DB	" bytes",13,10,"$"

; HWLIB.ASM: routines this chapter's programs share. It goes after a
; program's own code, since it makes bytes where it is included.

; Test for TEC-OS with ABI 5. Returns Z if the table's four bytes match,
; NZ if not. Changes AF, B, DE and HL.
CHKHW:	LD	HL,ABITAB	; signature, then the major version
	LD	DE,TAG		; what they must be
	LD	B,4		; a major of 6 fails as a wrong letter does
CHKH1:	LD	A,(DE)
	CP	(HL)
	RET	NZ		; NZ: not what TAG holds
	INC	HL		; on to the next of each
	INC	DE
	DJNZ	CHKH1
	RET			; Z from the last comparison

; End a program that found another system. Takes nothing, and returns to
; the CCP through the program's own return address.
NOTHW:	LD	DE,NOTMSG	; no board devices here, and no harm done
; Print the $-ended string at DE. A jump here prints and ends the program.
; Changes AF, BC, DE and HL.
SAY:	LD	C,9		; BDOS print string
	JP	BDOS		; its RET is this routine's

; Print the $-ended label at DE, then A in hex. Changes AF, BC and DE.
LABHEX:	PUSH	AF		; the value, across the BDOS call
	PUSH	HL		; the BDOS changes HL
	CALL	SAY
	POP	HL
	POP	AF		; on into HEX
; Print A as two hex digits, which also prints a BCD byte in decimal.
; Changes AF, BC and DE.
HEX:	PUSH	HL		; a caller may keep a value here
	PUSH	AF		; the low digit comes second
	RRCA			; the high digit down to bits 0 to 3
	RRCA
	RRCA
	RRCA
	CALL	NIBBLE		; the high digit
	POP	AF
	CALL	NIBBLE		; the low digit
	POP	HL
	RET

NIBBLE:	AND	$0F		; one digit
	ADD	A,'0'
	CP	'9'+1		; past 9: the letters start seven later
	JR	C,NIBB1
	ADD	A,7

	LD	C,2
	JP	BDOS		; its RET is this routine's

; DIGCLK: the time on the 7-segment digits, until a key.
BDOS	EQU	$0005
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
	CALL	CHKHW		; the numbers below hold only on ABI 5
	JP	NZ,NOTHW
LOOP:	LD	HL,PASSES	; the clock is read one pass in 32
	INC	(HL)
	LD	A,(HL)
	AND	31		; 0 on every 32nd pass
	CALL	Z,TOSEG
	LD	HL,DIGS		; one pass over the six digits
	LD	C,TNDIGIT
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	E,$FF		; BDOS direct input: a key, or 0
	LD	C,6
	CALL	BDOS
	OR	A
	JR	Z,LOOP		; no key: the digits need another pass
	RET			; DIGIT left them dark

; Read the clock and turn hours, minutes and seconds into six patterns at
; DIGS. Changes AF, BC, DE and HL; with no clock DIGS stays as it was.
TOSEG:	LD	HL,TIME		; seven BCD bytes, seconds first
	LD	B,0		; B = 0: read
	LD	C,TNRTC
	CALL	ABICALL
	RET	NZ		; status 2: no clock
	LD	DE,DIGS		; the leftmost digit's pattern first
	LD	A,(TIME+2)	; hours
	CALL	PAIR
	LD	A,(TIME+1)	; minutes
	CALL	PAIR
	LD	A,(TIME)	; seconds, and PAIR's RET ends TOSEG
; Store the two digits of the BCD byte in A as patterns at DE, which moves
; on by two. Changes AF, BC and HL.
PAIR:	PUSH	AF		; the units digit, for after the tens
	RRCA			; the tens digit down to bits 0 to 3
	RRCA
	RRCA
	RRCA
	CALL	SEG		; the tens
	POP	AF		; on into SEG for the units
; Store the low four bits of A as a pattern at DE, which moves on. Changes
; AF, BC and HL.
SEG:	AND	$0F		; one digit
	LD	C,A		; BC = the digit
	LD	B,0
	LD	HL,SEGTAB	; the digit's segments, one bit each
	ADD	HL,BC
	LD	A,(HL)
	LD	(DE),A		; into the row of six
	INC	DE
	RET

; The digits 0 to 9 as segment patterns.
SEGTAB:	DB	$EB,$28,$CD,$AD	; 0 to 3
	DB	$2E,$A7,$E7,$29	; 4 to 7
	DB	$EF,$AF		; 8 and 9
PASSES:	DB	31		; 31: the first pass reads the clock
DIGS:	DB	0,0,0,0,0,0
TIME:	DS	7
%INCLUDE "HWLIB.ASM"

; ROWS: wait for a key on the matrix keyboard, then print the eight rows
; and the joystick's byte.
BDOS	EQU	$0005
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
	CALL	CHKHW		; the numbers below hold only on ABI 5
	JP	NZ,NOTHW
	LD	C,TNINFO	; is there a matrix keyboard to wait for?
	CALL	ABICALL
	BIT	0,B		; INFO's matrix bit
	LD	DE,NOMTX
	JP	Z,SAY		; none: the wait would never end
WAIT:	CALL	SCAN		; until a key is down
	JR	Z,WAIT
	LD	C,TNJOY		; the same moment, read as the joystick
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	A,B		; its bits
	LD	(STICK),A	; printed after the rows
	LD	HL,BUF		; the eight rows, on one line
	LD	B,8
SHOW:	LD	A,(HL)		; one row's byte
	INC	HL
	PUSH	BC		; the count, across the printing
	CALL	HEX
	LD	E,' '		; BDOS console output
	LD	C,2
	PUSH	HL		; the BDOS changes HL
	CALL	BDOS
	POP	HL
	POP	BC
	DJNZ	SHOW
	LD	A,(STICK)	; JOY's bits
	LD	DE,MSGJOY
	CALL	LABHEX
	LD	DE,CRLF		; end the line
	CALL	SAY
DRAIN:	CALL	SCAN		; end only when every key is up
	JR	NZ,DRAIN
	RET

; Read the rows into BUF. Returns Z if no key is down, NZ if one is.
; Changes AF, BC, DE and HL.
SCAN:	LD	HL,BUF		; eight bytes, row 0 first
	LD	C,TNKEYS
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	HL,BUF		; OR the rows together
	LD	B,8
	XOR	A		; nothing seen yet
SCAN1:	OR	(HL)		; a key leaves a bit set
	INC	HL
	DJNZ	SCAN1
	OR	A		; Z if every row was 0
	RET

NOMTX:	DB	"no matrix keyboard",13,10,"$"
MSGJOY:	DB	" JOY $"
CRLF:	DB	13,10,"$"
BUF:	DS	8		; the rows, as KEYS leaves them
STICK:	DS	1		; JOY's byte
%INCLUDE "HWLIB.ASM"

; COUNT.SVC: count the characters that reach the BIOS's CONOUT, and publish
; the count in a record. REMOVE puts CONOUT back.
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
HDR:	DB	'D',SVCFMT,0,1	; magic, format, no dependencies, removable
	DW	0,0,0,0		; REMOVE, size, extra memory, relocation
	DB	2,2,2		; bytes added to the BDOS, BIOS, CCP stacks
	DW	0		; INIT
	DB	"COUNT   "	; the name SERVICES prints

; Point CONOUT at MYCO, keeping the old target. Returns HL = the record,
; carry clear. Changes AF, DE and HL.
INIT:	CALL	CONSLOT		; HL = the address held by CONOUT's JP
	LD	E,(HL)		; DE = that jump's target
	INC	HL
	LD	D,(HL)
	LD	(OLDCO),DE	; MYCO ends by jumping there
	LD	DE,MYCO		; the hook goes in last
	LD	(HL),D
	DEC	HL
	LD	(HL),E
	LD	HL,REC		; the record for the loader
	OR	A		; carry clear: installed
	RET

; Put CONOUT back. Returns carry clear. Changes AF, DE and HL.
REMOVE:	CALL	CONSLOT		; HL = the address held by CONOUT's JP
	LD	DE,(OLDCO)	; the target INIT saved
	LD	(HL),E
	INC	HL
	LD	(HL),D
	OR	A		; carry clear: removal goes ahead
	RET

; Find CONOUT's slot in the BIOS table. Returns HL = the address held by its
; JP. Changes F and DE.
CONSLOT:LD	HL,($0001)	; HL = the WBOOT entry
	LD	DE,9+1		; three entries on, and past the JP's opcode
	ADD	HL,DE
	RET

; The hook: count a character, then CONOUT as it was. Keeps every register
; for that jump.
MYCO:	PUSH	HL		; two bytes of the caller's stack
	LD	HL,(CHARS)	; the count, a word
	INC	HL
	LD	(CHARS),HL
	POP	HL		; C still holds the character
	DB	$C3		; JP to the entry replaced
OLDCO:	DW	0		; INIT fills this in

; The record's one entry. Returns HL = the count. Changes nothing else.
GETCNT:	LD	HL,(CHARS)
	RET

REC:	DW	0		; the link: the loader fills it
	DB	"COUNT   "	; the record's name
	DB	1		; its interface version
	DW	TABLE		; its entry table
TABLE:	JP	GETCNT		; offset 0: the count
CHARS:	DW	0		; the count itself

BDOS	EQU	$0005
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
	CALL	CHKHW		; the numbers below hold only on ABI 5
	JP	NZ,NOTHW	; prints and ends the program
	LD	DE,NAME		; the record's eight-byte name
	LD	B,1		; the least interface version
	LD	C,TNFIND	; the registry's find
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	DE,NONE
	JP	C,SAY		; carry: no such record, so print and end
	CALL	CALLHL		; offset 0 of the table: HL = the count
	PUSH	HL		; the low byte, for after the label
	LD	A,H		; the high byte first
	LD	DE,MSG		; the label
	CALL	LABHEX		; A is the high byte
	POP	HL
	LD	A,L		; the low byte, on the same line
	CALL	HEX
	LD	DE,CRLF		; end the line
	JP	SAY		; prints and ends the program

	DB	"record"
	DB	13,10,"$"

; RECS: list the registry, newest record first: each record's name, its
; interface version and the address of its entry table.
BDOS	EQU	$0005
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
	CALL	CHKHW		; the numbers below hold only on ABI 5
	JP	NZ,NOTHW
NEXT:	LD	A,(INDEX)	; the next record's number
	LD	B,A		; B = that number
	LD	C,TNLIST	; the registry's enumerate
	CALL	ABICALL
	RET	C		; carry: past the last record
	LD	A,(INDEX)	; the next one, for the next round
	INC	A
	LD	(INDEX),A
	CALL	SHOW		; one line for this record
	JR	NEXT		; until the carry above

; Print the record at HL on one line. Changes AF, BC, DE and HL.
SHOW:	INC	HL		; past the link word
	INC	HL		; HL = the name
	LD	B,8		; the eight bytes of the name
SHOW1:	LD	E,(HL)		; BDOS console output
	LD	C,2
	PUSH	BC		; the BDOS changes these
	PUSH	HL
	CALL	BDOS
	POP	HL
	POP	BC
	INC	HL		; the name's next byte
	DJNZ	SHOW1
	LD	A,(HL)		; the version, after the name
	INC	HL		; HL = the table's word
	LD	DE,VERS
	CALL	LABHEX		; LABHEX and HEX keep HL
	LD	E,(HL)		; DE = the table's address
	INC	HL
	LD	D,(HL)
	EX	DE,HL		; HL = it, which HEX keeps
	LD	A,H		; high byte first
	LD	DE,TABL
	CALL	LABHEX
	LD	A,L		; the low byte, on the same line
	CALL	HEX
	LD	DE,CRLF		; end the line
	JP	SAY		; its RET is this routine's

VERS:	DB	" version $"
TABL:	DB	" table $"
CRLF:	DB	13,10,"$"

; ARGS: prints the two FCBs and the command tail that the CCP leaves in
; page zero: each FCB's drive byte as a digit and its eleven name bytes,
; then the tail between brackets.
BDOS    EQU     $0005

        ORG     $0100
        LD      HL,$005C        ; the first FCB
        CALL    SHOWFCB
        LD      HL,$006C        ; the second
        CALL    SHOWFCB
        LD      A,'['
        CALL    PUT
        LD      HL,$0080        ; the tail's length, then its characters
        LD      B,(HL)
TAIL:   LD      A,B
        OR      A
        JR      Z,TEND
        INC     HL
        LD      A,(HL)
        CALL    PUT
        DEC     B
        JR      TAIL
TEND:   LD      A,']'
        JP      PUT

SHOWFCB:LD      A,(HL)          ; the drive: 0 for the current one
        ADD     A,'0'
        CALL    PUT
        LD      A,' '
        CALL    PUT
        LD      B,11            ; the name and type, as stored
NAME:   INC     HL
        LD      A,(HL)
        CALL    PUT
        DJNZ    NAME
        LD      A,13
        CALL    PUT
        LD      A,10

; Print A by function 2, keeping B and HL.
PUT:    PUSH    HL
        PUSH    BC
        LD      E,A
        LD      C,2
        CALL    BDOS
        POP     BC
        POP     HL
        RET

fences.text:
; VTEST: write four bytes to the PICO9918's VRAM and read them back through
; the graphics entries of the ROM's PICO9918 console.
BDOS	EQU	$0005
VRAM	EQU	$3000		; an address the text modes leave alone
%INCLUDE "ABI.INC"

	ORG	$0100
	CALL	CHKHW		; the numbers below hold only on ABI 5
	JP	NZ,NOTHW
	LD	DE,NAME		; the record's eight-byte name
	LD	B,2		; version 2 has the graphics entries
	LD	C,TNFIND	; the registry's find
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	DE,NONE
	JP	C,SAY		; carry: no such record, so print and end
	LD	(TABLE),HL	; good until this program exits
	LD	B,1		; claim the PICO9918
	LD	C,TNVIDEO
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	HL,VRAM		; PICOWR: BC bytes from DE to VRAM at HL
	LD	DE,DATA		; the bytes to write
	LD	BC,4
	LD	A,PICOWR	; the entry's offset in the table
	CALL	ENTRY
	LD	HL,VRAM		; PICORD: BC bytes from VRAM at HL to DE
	LD	DE,BACK		; where to put them
	LD	BC,4
	LD	A,PICORD	; the entry's offset in the table
	CALL	ENTRY
	LD	B,0		; give it back: the console's screen returns
	LD	C,TNVIDEO
	CALL	ABICALL
	LD	DE,BACK		; the four bytes, as text
	JP	SAY		; prints and ends the program

; Run the table's entry at offset A, with its arguments in BC, DE and HL.
; Changes what the entry changes.
ENTRY:	PUSH	HL		; the entry's HL
	PUSH	DE		; and its DE
	LD	E,A		; DE = the offset
	LD	D,0
	LD	HL,(TABLE)
	ADD	HL,DE		; HL = the entry's word
	LD	E,(HL)
	INC	HL
	LD	D,(HL)
	EX	DE,HL		; HL = the routine
	POP	DE		; the entry's DE back
	EX	(SP),HL		; the routine goes on the stack, HL comes back
	RET			; a jump to it, with HL free

TABLE:	DW	0		; the table, once found
NAME:	DB	"PICO    "	; the record to find
NONE:	DB	"no PICO "	; printed when there is no record
	DB	"record"
	DB	13,10,"$"
DATA:	DB	"VRAM"		; the four bytes to write
BACK:	DB	"????"		; PICORD fills these four
	DB	13,10,"$"
%INCLUDE "HWLIB.ASM"
